title: Ecological Momentary Assessment (Behavioral Science) for In-the-Wild Sycophancy Sampling

original_idea.body:
# Ecological Momentary Assessment (Behavioral Science) for In-the-Wild Sycophancy Sampling

**Problem:** Lab sycophancy benchmarks overstate robustness; real conversational pressure is what matters, but we lack a sampling methodology that captures honesty 'in context' rather than in artificial single-shot tests.

**Direction:** Transfer Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) from behavioral science: instead of a fixed benchmark, probe honesty at random moments embedded inside realistic synthetic multi-turn dialogues (drawn from public conversation datasets), inserting truth-probe turns at random conversational depths and contexts. Aggregate context-dependent honesty rates, capturing the 'in-the-wild' distribution the system card flagged.

**Why it matters:** Builds a realistic, context-embedded sycophancy measurement methodology directly responsive to the Opus 4.5 finding that benchmarks overstate robustness — achievable with public dialogue data and open models, no lab.

**Relevant context:** Claude Opus 4.5 system card: real conversational pressure reveals ~10% course-correction; benchmarks overstate robustness. SYCON measures multi-turn sycophancy (arXiv:2505.23840). EMA samples behavior in natural context in psychology.
